\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{فساد} (fasād)}{فساد (fasād)}]{\ar{فساد} (fasād) — corruption}

\label{lesson:AR-C388-fasad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a majority, then the Arabic for a minority.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{فساد}}
\textbf{\ar{فساد}} — \emph{fasād} — \textquotedblleft{}corruption\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تحدث} \ar{الناس} \ar{كثيرا} \ar{عن} \ar{الفساد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taḥaddatha an-nās kathīran ʿan al-fasād.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
People talked a lot about corruption.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{فساد}} (\emph{fasād}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-s-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to go bad, to be corrupt\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Fasād} is going bad: decay, and so corruption.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fasād}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fasād}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taḥaddatha an-nās kathīran ʿan al-fasād.} — People talked a lot about corruption.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a majority, then the Arabic for a minority, then say \emph{fasād} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{فساد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Corruption\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{رشوة} (rashwa)}{رشوة (rashwa)}]{\ar{رشوة} (rashwa) — a bribe}

\label{lesson:AR-C388-rashwa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a minority, then the Arabic for corruption.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{رشوة}}
\textbf{\ar{رشوة}} — \emph{rashwa} — \textquotedblleft{}a bribe\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{رفض} \ar{الموظف} \ar{الرشوة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rafaḍa al-muwaẓẓaf ar-rashwa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The employee refused the bribe.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{رشوة}} (\emph{rashwa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-sh-w}, \textquotedblleft{}a well rope\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is usually linked with \emph{rishāʾ}, a well rope: a bribe is the rope let down to draw up what one wants.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a minority, then the Arabic for corruption, then say \emph{rashwa} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{إصلاح} (iṣlāḥ)}{إصلاح (iṣlāḥ)}]{\ar{إصلاح} (iṣlāḥ) — reform}

\label{lesson:AR-C388-islah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for corruption, then the Arabic for a bribe.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{إصلاح}}
\textbf{\ar{إصلاح}} — \emph{iṣlāḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}reform\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تحتاج} \ar{الشركة} \ar{إلى} \ar{إصلاح} \ar{كبير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taḥtāju ash-sharika ilā iṣlāḥ kabīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The company needs major reform.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{إصلاح}} (\emph{iṣlāḥ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṣ-l-ḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}to be good, right\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Iṣlāḥ} is the Form IV verbal noun of \emph{aṣlaḥa}, to put right: repair, reform.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taḥtāju ash-sharika ilā iṣlāḥ kabīr.} — The company needs major reform.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for corruption, then the Arabic for a bribe, then say \emph{iṣlāḥ} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{انتهك} (intahaka)}{انتهك (intahaka)}]{\ar{انتهك} (intahaka) — to violate}

\label{lesson:AR-C388-intahaka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a bribe, then the Arabic for reform.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{انتهك}}
\textbf{\ar{انتهك}} — \emph{intahaka} — \textquotedblleft{}to violate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{انتهك} \ar{الجيران} \ar{حقنا} \ar{في} \ar{النوم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{intahaka al-jīrān ḥaqqanā fī an-nawm.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The neighbours violated our right to sleep.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينتهك}, \emph{yantahik}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{انتهك}} (\emph{intahaka}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-h-k}, \textquotedblleft{}to wear out, to exhaust\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VIII; Lane gives it for violating what is held sacred: to violate.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intahaka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intahaka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intahaka al-jīrān ḥaqqanā fī an-nawm.} — The neighbours violated our right to sleep.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a bribe, then the Arabic for reform, then say \emph{intahaka} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استغل} (istaghalla)}{استغل (istaghalla)}]{\ar{استغل} (istaghalla) — to exploit}

\label{lesson:AR-C388-istaghalla}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for reform, then the Arabic for to violate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استغل}}
\textbf{\ar{استغل}} — \emph{istaghalla} — \textquotedblleft{}to exploit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{استغل} \ar{صاحب} \ar{المصنع} \ar{العمال}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{istaghalla ṣāḥib al-maṣnaʿ al-ʿummāl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The factory owner exploited the workers.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يستغل}, \emph{yastaghill}.

Also, neutrally, to make use of: \ar{استغل} \ar{الوقت}, made good use of the time.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{استغل}} (\emph{istaghalla}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{gh-l-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to yield produce\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form X, to seek the yield of a thing: to make use of it, or to exploit it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istaghalla}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istaghalla}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istaghalla ṣāḥib al-maṣnaʿ al-ʿummāl.} — The factory owner exploited the workers.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for reform, then the Arabic for to violate, then say \emph{istaghalla} again
\end{itemize}
